title: Coalition can attain an output
statement: Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a set of coordinates, let $b\in\{−1,1\}$, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The coalition of coordinates in $J$ can attain output $b$ from $x$ if there is an input $y$ agreeing with $x$ outside $J$ such that $f(y)=b$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates
